text: These are actual project-source excerpts explaining the work behind the interface.
A light editor-style layout makes the key code and responsibilities easier to read.
Compose Multiplatform is a declarative UI framework for Kotlin.
State defines the UI, buttons receive input, and the Rust engine handles pixels.
The pen pointer loads an image resource and sizes it from the base display density.
It connects to the system pointer service without adding a ring to the artwork.
Canvas input enters the coordination layer, with pen and touch sharing editing boundaries.
The input queue is bounded, and background work returns results to the display layer.
The Rust engine processes strokes and pixels, including closed-shape fills.
These canvas results come from the real engine, not a prerecorded effect animation.
The canvas is organized into tiles, so changed areas can be sent to the interface.
Shared unchanged pixels avoid repeated copying and retain earlier content for every undo.
History and project files also belong to the engine; the UI coordinates user actions.
Rust handles that work in the background; it is not all GPU computation.
Basic vectors and drawing assistants use the same path from parameters to previews.
Separating state from pixel work makes edits easier to preview and commit.
